author: ATAMANCZ

status.label: Needs specific evidence
status.detail: The canonical stuck-Ctrl issue needs a failure-time trace and exact mappings.

next_action.label: Request failure-time Ctrl diagnostics
next_action.reason: Capture state before any recovery action clears it.

judgment.rationale: Multiple current confirmations establish a real intermittent state bug, but the trigger is not deterministic and differs between local and RDP scenarios. A failure-time diagnostic plus the exact remap set is needed to distinguish stale modifier bookkeeping from RDP/focus transitions.
evidence: Reports span 0.84.0 through 0.100.2 and several machines.
On-screen keyboard input is also affected, while Keyboard Manager-defined Ctrl remaps can continue to work.
Issues 35404, 45897, 41668, 34523, 35836, and 39705 were closed as duplicates of this issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a current failure-time /bugreport archive, exported remap configuration, and precise RDP/focus transition state.

fix_assessment.rationale: The failure is clearly in the Keyboard Manager path, but public evidence does not isolate the state transition sufficiently to choose a safe code change.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager intermittently leaves Ctrl visible to its hook but ineffective for normal application shortcuts; toggling Keyboard Manager, leaving the keyboard idle, or changing RDP focus can temporarily recover it.
known_information: Ctrl shortcuts degrade to plain letters after minutes or hours; restarting or toggling Keyboard Manager restores them.
A current reporter reproduces on 0.100.2 with Windows 11 and RDP full-screen transitions.
Keyboard Manager mappings such as Ctrl+H can still execute while ordinary Ctrl shortcuts fail.
inferences: The engine may retain an inconsistent physical/logical Ctrl state after a focus, RDP, or swallowed-event transition.
Different reports may share a state-cleanup failure even though their immediate triggers differ.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is the canonical target for several duplicate stuck-modifier reports. Current code has several modifier reset paths, so a trace captured while the state is broken is more discriminating than another generic description.
initial_investigation: Verified six later issues were explicitly closed as duplicates of #34714.
Reviewed current KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp modifier reset and state cleanup paths, including recent stuck-modifier fixes; the latest report postdates those fixes.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive captured while Ctrl shortcuts are failing, before toggling Keyboard Manager or leaving/re-entering RDP.
information_gaps.why_needed: It can correlate the failure with hook state, module restarts, focus/session transitions, and the current build.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: While the failure is present, add a comment containing /bugreport before restarting or toggling PowerToys.

information_gaps.information: The exact Keyboard Manager remap set in effect on the affected machine.
information_gaps.why_needed: The active source/target modifiers determine which state machine and cleanup branch must be inspected.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Export or screenshot the Keyboard Manager mappings, redacting unrelated text-expansion contents if any.

information_gaps.information: Whether the failure immediately follows an RDP full-screen transition, unlock, sleep/wake, elevated window, or ordinary local typing.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates session/focus event loss from a purely local shortcut-sequencing bug.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: When it next occurs, note the immediately preceding transition and whether the on-screen keyboard Ctrl key changes state.

comment.body:
Thanks for the current-version confirmations and the RDP sequence already documented. The remaining gap is the exact state at the moment Ctrl stops reaching normal applications. Please provide:
- A comment containing `/bugreport` while the failure is still present, before toggling Keyboard Manager, leaving RDP, or restarting PowerToys.
- The exact Keyboard Manager remaps active at that time (an export or screenshots are sufficient).
- Whether the last transition was RDP full-screen/windowed, lock/unlock, sleep/wake, an elevated window, or ordinary local typing, and what the on-screen keyboard shows for Ctrl.
These details will distinguish stale modifier bookkeeping from a lost session/focus key-up event.

title: keyboard manager steals completely CTRL after few hours of running
